items.title: AI Just Lost The Election. Bigger Models Are Coming Anyway.
items.vendor_flag: No guest. Hosts are enthusiastic users of OpenAI and Anthropic models; GPT 6.2 Astra and Fable 5.5 are rumours at recording. The $18 to 20 million bounty comparison and the data centre vote count are relayed off the cuff (Fast Company named for the votes) and not verified.
items.reader_fit: Low. Mostly AI news and gadgets; a UK recruiter gets a transferable scout-then-review agent pattern and context on data centre backlash, nothing recruiting-specific.

points.claim: OpenAI used a fleet of small agents then reviewer agents to find and patch Linux kernel bugs, at a fraction of bounty cost.
points.evidence: 948 local privilege escalation patches, $1.2 million, 2,000 plus findings, about 30 million lines of code
points.quote: They had these tiny little agents go out, find what could be attack surfaces.

points.claim: Local US ballot measures on data centres almost all failed; host reads it as rejection of AI being forced on people.
points.evidence: 40 plus data centre votes, only one won (Fast Company, as relayed)

points.claim: Host's asks of frontier labs: AI education and re-education for adults, plus a cross-party coalition.
points.evidence: Gavin: three things frontier companies can do
points.quote: it's really time for these companies to get serious about AI education

points.claim: A smart AI rewriting a small AI's weights improved it on benchmarks, early stage only.
points.evidence: 40 to 50% better on certain math benchmarks (weight space programming paper)
points.quote: they found that it did like 40 to 50% better on certain math benchmarks

points.claim: Practical AI video dialogue prompt tip relayed from second_bassoon.
points.evidence: Break long lines into shorter ones; use bodily actions as punctuation
points.quote: Break long lines into shorter ones with intentional pauses.

items.title: Why PMs are suddenly valuable again
items.guest_line: Tulsee Doshi · Head of Product, Gemini @ Google
items.vendor_flag: Guest is the vendor behind Gemini and promotes Gemini 4 and Google products; her own '14 products above a billion users' stat is flagged by her as unchecked.
items.reader_fit: Medium. Useful for UK recruiters hiring or advising on PMs and AI product roles: concrete hiring signals and a small-eval starting method.

points.claim: Start your first eval tiny, with your own judgement as the rater.
points.evidence: five prompts to start, mini eval of about 20 prompts
points.quote: start with even just five prompts

points.claim: Build roughly 60% that works now and aim the rest at capabilities models are close to unlocking.
points.evidence: 60-20-20 rule; she says numbers are fungible
points.quote: build such that like 60% of what you've built works now

points.claim: Hiring signal for research PMs: opinionated daily model users who can build evals and adapt.
points.evidence: PMs who understand model vibes, roll up sleeves, build an eval; roadmap rewritten after two months
points.quote: I want PMs who have an opinion

points.claim: Delegate repeatable work to AI, keep insight human.
points.evidence: twice rule; insight from human, data from model
points.quote: if you have to do something twice, do you need to do it yourself?

points.claim: Her team is running a two-day November workshop for PMs to build with tools.
